key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces, reducing interfacial recombination and enabling 25.86% power conversion efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular passivation chemistry can improve electron extraction into C60 and guide interface design for methylammonium-free solar cells.
method: Use neutral ethylenediamine to chelate undercoordinated metals and remove excess surface tin.
Compare reconstruction with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide passivation and subsequent deprotonation.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation energetics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% device efficiency, suppressed interfacial nonradiative recombination, and simulations linking subsurface iodide vacancies to easier deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term stability and manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the reconstructed interface are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
